keyTakeaways: Poe never wrote the word Halloween: a search of all five Raven Edition volumes, about 444,000 words, finds zero matches; he died on 7 October 1849.
Twelve Halloween-ready Poe lines check out verbatim, from "The Raven" (29 January 1845) to "Spirits of the Dead" (1827).
At least 8 popular "Poe quotes" are fake, reworded or misdated, including "mysterious as a cat" and the 1848 "horrible sanity" letter often dated 1846.

faqs.question: Which Poe poem is set in October?
faqs.answer: "Ulalume", first printed in December 1847, is set on an October night by "the dank tarn of Auber" in a "ghoul-haunted woodland". It is the nearest Poe comes to the Halloween season, since the word Halloween never appears in his collected works.

faqs.question: What is the most famous Poe quote for Halloween?
faqs.answer: "Deep into that darkness peering, long I stood there wondering, fearing" from "The Raven", first printed on 29 January 1845, is the one most people reach for. The raven's single word, "Nevermore", is the shortest option.

faqs.question: Did Poe really say "I wish I could write as mysterious as a cat"?
faqs.answer: No. The line does not appear anywhere in the Raven Edition, and the Poe Museum in Richmond lists it as one of the most misattributed Poe quotes. Use a real line from "The Raven" or "The Tell-Tale Heart" instead.

faqs.question: Is "Believe nothing you hear, and only one half that you see" a real Poe quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, though usually reworded. It comes from "The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether", printed in Graham's Magazine in November 1845; the popular version swaps the order to "believe only half of what you see".

faqs.question: When did Poe write "I became insane, with long intervals of horrible sanity"?
faqs.answer: In a letter to George W. Eveleth dated 4 January 1848, as transcribed by the Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore. Some quote lists date it 1846, which is wrong, and in context he is describing six years of his wife's illness.

faqs.question: What is a short Poe quote for an Instagram caption?
faqs.answer: "It is the beating of his hideous heart!" from "The Tell-Tale Heart" (January 1843) is 8 words, and "Lo! 'tis a gala night / Within the lonesome latter years!" from "The Conqueror Worm" (January 1843) is 10. Both fit a phone screen without wrapping into a paragraph.

faqs.question: Is Edgar Allan Poe's writing in the public domain?
faqs.answer: Yes. Poe died in 1849 and everything he published appeared between 1827 and 1849, so his poems, tales and letters are out of copyright and can be quoted on cards, captions and pages. Modern editions' notes and introductions may still be protected.

faqs.question: How can I check whether a Poe quote is real?
faqs.answer: Search five words in a row from the quote inside the Raven Edition text on Project Gutenberg, and check the Poe Society of Baltimore for the work and first printing date. If a quote circulates with no work and no year, treat it as suspect until you find it.

faqs.question: Are Poe quotes okay for kids at Halloween?
faqs.answer: Mostly not for young children. "The Tell-Tale Heart" ends in a murder confession and "The Premature Burial" is about being buried alive, so keep those lines for teenagers and adults.

faqs.question: Can I put a Poe quote on a Halloween card for my partner?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one line at the top of a personal letter rather than a list. SubhSandesh's interactive Halloween card shows your letter by flashlight in a dark attic, and the premium page adds a voice note of up to 60 seconds if you would rather read the stanza aloud.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Edgar Allan Poe Halloween Quotes, Each Checked Against His Text

The Edgar Allan Poe Halloween quotes worth using are lines he actually printed, such as "Deep into that darkness peering" from "The Raven" (1845) or the last sentence of "The Masque of the Red Death" (1842). Fit matters too: 48.3% of pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and each page averages 11.1 views, so a quote gets reread on a small screen.

We checked every line below against the five-volume Raven Edition of Poe's works and the Poe Society's dating. One surprise: Poe never wrote the word "Halloween". Below are 12 verified lines with work and year, 8 popular "Poe quotes" that are fake, reworded or misdated, a table of where each fits, and when a Poe line is the wrong choice.

## Did Edgar Allan Poe ever write about Halloween?

No: we searched the full text of the Raven Edition on [Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2148), about 444,000 words across five volumes including the editors' notes, for "Halloween", "Hallowe'en" and "All Hallows". There were zero matches. Poe died in Baltimore on 7 October 1849, 24 days before the holiday.

So every "Poe Halloween quote" is a line borrowed for the season. The closest he came is October: "Ulalume", first printed in December 1847, is set on an October night. Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027, and the lines below suit either.

## 12 verified Poe quotes for Halloween, with work and year

Each group gives the same three things in the same order: the exact words, the first printing as dated by the Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore, and the best use. Spelling and punctuation follow the Raven Edition, dashes included.

### 1. "The Raven" (first printed 29 January 1845)

- "Deep into that darkness peering, long I stood there wondering, fearing, / Doubting, dreaming dreams no mortal ever dared to dream before;"
- "And each separate dying ember wrought its ghost upon the floor."
- "'Prophet!' said I, 'thing of evil!—prophet still, if bird or devil!—'"

The poem ran in the New York *Evening Mirror* that day, ahead of a magazine issue dated February 1845. The first line is the classic caption for a candlelit photo; the ember line is 11 words, short enough for a card.

### 2. "The Tell-Tale Heart" (January 1843)

- "True!—nervous—very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am; but why will you say that I am mad?"
- "It is the beating of his hideous heart!"

The first is the story's opening sentence (18 words) and the second is its last line (8 words). The Poe Society dates the first printing to January 1843. Use the closing line under a costume photo with a fake heart prop; it reads as a punchline only if the viewer knows the story.

### 3. "The Masque of the Red Death" (May 1842)

- "The 'Red Death' had long devastated the country."
- "And Darkness and Decay and the Red Death held illimitable dominion over all."

The story first ran as "The Mask of the Red Death. A Fantasy." in May 1842. A 2002 essay in the CDC journal *Emerging Infectious Diseases*, [Vora and Ramanan's "Ebola-Poe"](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC2738525), reads its symptoms as close to a filovirus haemorrhagic fever, noting Poe could not have known Ebola or Marburg. The closing line (13 words) is the strongest masquerade-party caption Poe wrote.

### 4. "The Premature Burial" (31 July 1844) and "Eleonora" (1841)

- "The boundaries which divide Life from Death are at best shadowy and vague. Who shall say where the one ends, and where the other begins?"
- "They who dream by day are cognizant of many things which escape those who dream only by night."

The burial line (25 words) is the best Poe sentence for Halloween's old idea of a thin border between the living and the dead. The "Eleonora" line is often printed with "Those" in place of "They"; the Raven Edition reads "They". It appeared in *The Gift* for 1842, issued around September 1841.

### 5. Three poems: "Ulalume" (1847), "The Conqueror Worm" (1843), "Spirits of the Dead" (1827)

- "It was down by the dank tarn of Auber, / In the ghoul-haunted woodland of Weir."
- "Lo! 'tis a gala night / Within the lonesome latter years!"
- "Thy soul shall find itself alone / 'Mid dark thoughts of the grey tomb-stone—"

"The Conqueror Worm" was first printed in *Graham's Magazine* in January 1843, then set inside "Ligeia" in February 1845. "Spirits of the Dead" began as "Visit of the Dead" in Poe's first book, *Tamerlane and Other Poems* (1827), printed when he was 18. The "gala night" couplet is 10 words, the shortest here.

## 8 "Poe quotes" that are fake, reworded or misdated

The [Poe Museum's list of misattributions](https://poemuseum.org/did-poe-really-say-that/) says most Poe quotes on the internet are not his. We checked each line below against the same five volumes and Poe's letters.

- **"I wish I could write as mysterious as a cat."** Not Poe. Zero matches in the Raven Edition, and the Poe Museum calls it one of the most misattributed lines. It circulates every October beside black-cat photos.
- **"Believe only half of what you see and nothing that you hear."** Reworded. The real line, from "The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether" (*Graham's*, November 1845), is "Believe nothing you hear, and only one-half that you see."
- **"That which you mistake for madness is but an over acuteness of the senses."** Reworded. "The Tell-Tale Heart" reads "what you mistake for madness is but over-acuteness of the sense"; "sense" is singular.
- **"There is no exquisite beauty without some strangeness in the proportion."** Real Poe, in "Ligeia" (1838), but he is quoting Francis Bacon, and loosely. Bacon's 1625 essay "Of Beauty" says "There is no excellent beauty, that hath not some strangeness in the proportion."
- **"I became insane, with long intervals of horrible sanity."** Genuine, but often dated 1846. The Poe Society's text of the [letter to George W. Eveleth](https://www.eapoe.org/works/letters/p4801040.htm) is dated 4 January 1848, and the line describes six years of his wife's illness, not a joke.
- **"I do not suffer from insanity, I enjoy every minute of it."** Not Poe. The Poe Museum traced it to joke books, the earliest from 1996.
- **"Sometimes I'm terrified of my heart..."** Not Edgar Allan Poe. It is a lyric by the singer Poe, a different person entirely.
- **"All religion, my friend, is simply evolved out of fraud, fear, greed, imagination, and poetry."** Not Poe. The Poe Museum traces it to the biographer John Alexander Joyce.

A fast test before you post: open the Raven Edition text on Gutenberg and search the page for five words in a row from the quote. A line that comes with no work and no year is the one to doubt.

## Which Poe quote fits where?

This compares four common uses with the verified line we would pick for each. Word counts are our own count of the line as printed above.

| Where it goes | Line to use | Work, first printed | Words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Instagram caption | "Lo! 'tis a gala night / Within the lonesome latter years!" | "The Conqueror Worm", January 1843 | 10 |
| Costume photo | "It is the beating of his hideous heart!" | "The Tell-Tale Heart", January 1843 | 8 |
| Card or letter | "The boundaries which divide Life from Death are at best shadowy and vague..." | "The Premature Burial", July 1844 | 25 |
| Party invitation | "And Darkness and Decay and the Red Death held illimitable dominion over all." | "The Masque of the Red Death", May 1842 | 13 |

Short lines win on phones. With nearly half of shared pages opened on one, keep captions under 15 words and save the 25-word sentence for a card or letter.

## Putting one Poe line on a Halloween page for one person

A Poe quote works best as a single line inside a longer message to someone who likes him, rather than a list. Our two Halloween templates are greeting pages for one person, with partner, bestie, family or kids modes. They are not party invitations for a crowd, and the interface is in English.

The [interactive Halloween card with photos and music](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about five minutes to make: your person knocks three times on a little haunted house, carves a jack-o'-lantern until your chosen word glows, and reads your letter by flashlight in a dark attic. Put the Poe line at the top of that letter; the card holds up to six photos and ends with "Will you be my boo?" and a Boo License sized 1080×1920.

The [premium cinematic Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about ten minutes and suits a reader who wants more: a ghost pops out of a haunted mailbox with your letter, a voice note up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and a letter up to 3,000 characters. It can stay locked until a time you set, such as 31 October at dusk, and it has one reply box. Reading "The Raven" stanza aloud into that voice note is the Poe move.

If they would rather hear you than read you, a [radio-style dedication page with your voice](https://subhsandesh.in/dedication) lets you introduce a song yourself, with a Poe line as the opening words. Whichever you choose, 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it; do it if your letter mentions anything private.

## When a Poe quote is the wrong choice

Skip Poe when your reader is grieving. His mother, his foster mother and his wife all died of tuberculosis, as Vora and Ramanan note in their 2002 essay, and his best lines are about the dead staying close. For someone recently bereaved, a cosier October line lands better.

Skip him for young children too. "The Tell-Tale Heart" ends in a murder confession and "The Premature Burial" is about being buried alive; neither suits a class of seven-year-olds. Keep his madness lines away from jokes about a friend's real mental health, because the 1848 letter shows Poe himself meant them seriously.

Poe on a greeting page also fails for a group. Our templates speak to one person; for a party of 20, a printed invitation or group chat works better.
